item.description:
Binary search

  • Search the answer space: Find the smallest or largest answer satisfying a monotonic condition—one whose truth value changes at most once as candidate answers increase. The input itself need not be sorted. Example: LeetCode#875: Koko Eating Bananas.

item.title: HTTP: The Language of the Web
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Tanviruzzaman
item.description:
HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol) is a stateless, human-readable application-layer protocol that operates on a client-server request-response model. A client uses URLs to locate resources and send requests to a server, which processes them and returns responses to transmit hypermedia and data across the web.

Request

GET /hello HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com

Response

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/plain
Content-Length: 13

Hello, world!

The client requests /hello. The server responds with 200 OK and a 13-byte text body. A blank line separates the headers from the body.

item.title: Good habits, bad habits
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Tanviruzzaman
item.description:
Habits automate familiar routines, freeing attention and deliberate effort for tasks that need them.

A habit is a learned (cue, response) association built through repetition, often supported by immediate reward. Lowering friction makes repetition easier—reducing the “activation energy” to act. Once established, the cue can prompt a response with little mental effort, even when the original reward is no longer valued. Such routines can escape notice; tracking can reveal them and help us decide what to preserve or change.

Sources

  • Good Habits, Bad Habits by Wendy Wood
  • Habit scorecard

item.title: Fundamental units
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Tanviruzzaman
item.description:
There are three fundamental units (of time, distance, and mass) and all other units of measurement are some combination of these three. First we define the unit of time–one second; we use second to define the unit of distance–one meter; and we use both second and meter to define the unit of mass–one kilogram.

We want these units to be stable, universal, and reproducible. What that means is: ten seconds should mean exactly the same duration today and 1000 years from now, here and anywhere else, and anyone with the right equipment should be able to reproduce that ten-second duration independently.

Second

One second is the duration of exactly 9,192,631,770 cycles of microwave radiation resonant with the unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition of a cesium-133 atom.

More…
Why exactly 9,192,631,770 cycles?

To preserve the duration of the second already in use.

Why cesium-133?

Cesium-133 has a stable, reproducible resonance that scientists can measure precisely using microwave electronics.

Why use a vacuum?

A vacuum reduces collisions with surrounding gas, which could disturb the atoms and shift their resonance frequency.

Meter

One meter is the distance light travels in a vacuum in exactly of a second.

More…

Kilogram

One kilogram is the mass that makes Planck’s constant exactly

item.title: Centripetal acceleration in uniform circular motion

item.description:
To understand how acceleration affects velocity, it is useful to think of acceleration vector having just two components: one parallel to the velocity vector and the other perpendicular to the velocity vector.
